attributes.summary: Initial T1 authored: divergent-sources-of-truth problem statement, git-as-source-of-truth premise, methodology overview, draft event ontology (26 events in 5+1 categories, 7 entity types), sequential per-commit extraction approach, three-tier storage (events.jsonl + SQLite + snapshots), pre-commit hook lifecycle, plugin structure outline.

Tier altitudes clarified: T1/T2 are Claude co-work altitude (planning), T3 is Claude Code altitude (execution). T1 framed as the anti-bottom-up grounding layer that ensures downstream agents land with proper why / audience / outcomes orientation. Three load-bearing reasons for tiered structure made explicit: different agents read different tiers, change frequency differs by tier, decisions cascade downward not upward.

Tier 0 added as optional commercial layer: the proposal sent to a client or stakeholder (budget, timeframe, expectations, scope agreement). Pre-project, not required, but useful commercial background for agents when it exists.

Lettered-workstream nomenclature introduced: XT1/XT2/XT3 for crosscut concerns (X = crosscut), PT1/PT2/PT3 (and AT, BT, etc.) for side quests (any letter other than X). Letter prefix identifies the workstream; T-number denotes altitude. Main spine is unprefixed. Corrects the original 'multiple T1 plans' framing — there is one main T1 plus zero or more lettered workstreams, each with its own 1/2/3 tree.

Append-only / supersede-don't-delete discipline made explicit. Plans grow by addition (extension at end-of-file) or are marked superseded/cancelled/parked; never deleted. Provenance preserved so agents can see what was tried and rejected, avoiding re-proposing abandoned approaches.

Ontology simplification round one: `entity.changed` dropped (collapsed into `entity.extended` — plan changes are inherently additive by design; the refactor/redirect/reframe sub-discriminator was redundant with supersession-with-multiple-IDs). `entity.reverted` dropped (redundant with `entity.reopened` + decision). Event count drops from 26 to 24.

Discovery as entity type dropped from scope. Decisions adequately cover the structured rationale capture for now; discoveries about libraries, agent behaviours, and methodology gotchas are useful but orthogonal to project history tracking. Documented in §7 Out of scope; may be revisited as a separate concern later.

`relationship.reattached` event type added to handle orphan resolution when a parent is superseded. Child moves from old parent to new parent. Conceptually a rebase primitive for the planning graph. Event count returns to 25 (24 + 1).

Orphan status defined as a derived state (parent dead, child unresolved), not directly emitted as an event. Cleared by `relationship.reattached`, `entity.cancelled`, or `entity.superseded`. Avoids event-cascade noise on parent supersession; the projection layer surfaces orphans naturally from graph state.

Derived entity state taxonomy formalised: live (created, extended, progressed, reopened) / dormant (parked) / dead (completed, cancelled, superseded) / orphaned (parent dead, unresolved) / unknown (ambiguous chain). Each entity lifecycle event mapped to its implied derived state.

Pre-commit hook responsibility split: pre-commit only extracts events (no cleanliness gating, allowing sub-agents to commit freely on branches). Pre-merge-to-main hook runs the projection-must-be-clean gate (orphans, fulcrum-without-decision, configurable smells). Override path via explicit decision event acknowledging acknowledged-and-deferred mess.

Snapshot format extended to include per-entity event-type sequence (just type names, not full payloads). The sequence pattern itself is a signal — short sequence means simple backstory the agent can act on without deeper digging; long sequences with flapping closures or unclosed blockers warrant investigation. Surfaced in snapshot summary.md as highlighted patterns.

SQLite confirmed as cache backend for this scale. Swap-out trigger documented: if more than ~30% of projection queries require multi-hop traversal (depth ≥ 3) or relationship-pattern matching becomes a primary projection surface, evaluate embedded graph engines with GQL/Cypher support (KuzuDB, Cozo). GQL standardisation reduces historical graph-engine lock-in risk.

Plan-vs-tracker rebalance: structured rationale lives in the tracker (events); prose lives in plan files. Separate decisions-log artefact dissolves — decision text folds naturally into plan prose where it matters, and structured capture happens via the tracker. Plans become lighter; bureaucracy around 'where do I put this decision' disappears.

Major ontology refactor. Decisions reframed as arc metadata (not graph nodes, not entities) — text annotations on events. Persons reframed as field values (the actor field on events), not graph nodes. Entity types reduced from 7 to 5 (plan, blocker, hitl-question, implicit-work, inbox-item). The original 3-event decision triad (ratified/referenced/superseded) collapsed into a single unified `decision` event carrying text plus an `event_ids[]` array of arcs it explains; many arcs can reference the same decision. Final event count: 23.

Decision granularity rule: only the 5 fulcrum events require paired decisions — entity.renamed, entity.parked, entity.cancelled, entity.superseded, entity.reopened. All other events are self-documenting by nature: decisions, blockers, verifications and relationships carry their meaning intrinsically; created/extended/progressed/completed are natural lifecycle progressions. Decisions remain optional on any non-fulcrum event when justification is worth capturing structurally.

Verification ontology flagged for future review as overwrought. The current 4-event category (claimed/tested/skipped/failed) may be replaceable by a cleaner 2-event split: probably-closed (any agent, after attempting tests where possible) and actually-closed (separate agent or human confirms — different actor required). Not changing now; revisit when M1 dogfooding surfaces real friction.

HTML view design committed: dynamic-from-projection.json rather than static-rebuild-per-event. Pure HTML + vanilla JS + JSON data file, no build step. Template loads projection on demand; time-travel via snapshot selector reads frozen projection.json from snapshots dir. Fulcrum arcs are clickable to reveal decision text. Two priority views: entity state board (grouped by derived state) and plan hierarchy tree.

Artefact strategy framed: developer audience; suggested as an npm-installable package bundling CLI scripts and Claude plugin files in one install. Works in both Claude Code and Claude Cowork (Cowork is filesystem-accessing, not browser-only — Claude Code with reduced jargon for less-technical users). Cowork especially useful at T1/T2 (project-management) altitude. Naming TBD — `apt` rejected due to Debian/Ubuntu namespace collision. Details deferred to T2 (M4 packaging milestone).

Themes (Tn) and milestones (Mn) recognised as orthogonal partitioning axes, not alternatives. Both become first-class plan kinds, discriminated by a `plan_kind: thematic | milestone` attribute on the `plan` entity. Every T3 has a thematic parent (its T2, whether on main spine or a lettered workstream) and a milestone target (its Mn). Mn plans get sequential IDs of the form M<n>-<slug>. Milestone membership lives in T3 frontmatter, not as a graph relationship event — scheduling adjusts naturally as work shapes up.

Plan ID naming convention made explicit: thematic plan IDs include the tier prefix as part of the slug (e.g., `T1-top-level`, `T2-ontology`, `XT2-analytics`). Previously implicit — main-spine T1 was named just `top-level` without the prefix, inconsistent with the lettered-workstream and milestone forms. Now uniform: every thematic plan ID is `<tier_prefix>T<tier>-<slug>`. Existing events updated in-place from `top-level` to `T1-top-level` (permitted under schema 0.0.0-prehistoric). T1 doc gains YAML frontmatter declaring the canonical id.

Identity convention tightened: (a) plan filenames are now load-bearing — must equal `entity_id` + `.md` extension; the T1 doc renamed from `01-top-level.md` to `T1-top-level.md`. (b) `tier_prefix` attribute made optional — omitted entirely for main-spine plans, present only on lettered workstreams (X for crosscut, P/A/etc. for side quests). T1 YAML frontmatter accordingly drops the `tier_prefix: ""` line; existing `entity.created` event's attributes block also sheds the empty `tier_prefix`. CLAUDE.md filename-convention block updated to reflect the new T1/T2/T3/Mn/lettered-workstream forms.

Ontology specification format added as open question §5.11. Currently the ontology lives only as prose in T1 §4. Automated extraction (M2 onward) needs formal capture the extractor can validate against. Default plan: JSON Schema as the standard, with `schemas/events.schema.json` (and possibly entity / plan-frontmatter schemas) landed during M1. The per-event `schema_version` field will tie each event to a versioned schema file.

attributes.summary: Commit metadata refactored off individual events. Previously each event carried a `commit_meta` sub-object (author / date / message_first_line), redundant when many events come from a single commit. Now `commit_meta` is carried only on the terminal `commit.recorded` event of each commit's event group. Positional rollup: all events between the previous `commit.recorded` (or log start) and the next `commit.recorded` belong to that closing event. Reduces per-commit event-log size meaningfully when commits emit dozens of events. T1 §4.2 updated to document the convention; `entity_type` / `entity_id` made optional for the meta-category `commit.recorded` (it has no subject entity).

attributes.title: Methodology rule: agents must emit entity.created for plans
attributes.summary: When emitting events for a plan that doesn't already exist in events.jsonl, agents must include an entity.created event with the plan's frontmatter as attributes — even for one-event lifecycles. The cache builder materialises entities.attributes only from entity.created; without it, downstream projections lose plan_kind/tier/t2_parent/milestone and entities get mis-routed (e.g. fell through to 'Other' swimlane in the flow view). Workaround: cache-build now reads frontmatter as fallback.

HTML view polish: workstreams-flow third view gained a resizable right sidebar replacing the bottom detail panel. Click an entity name on the left → its plan/inbox markdown renders in the sidebar (marked.js via CDN, frontmatter stripped). Click a node → event details. Drag handle between SVG and sidebar resizes. Swimlane labels promoted to uppercase + bold with proper top-band spacing (no more squish). Entity-label cursor switched from `help` (question-mark) to `pointer` since click now does something useful.

cache-build.py gained a frontmatter fallback: for plan entities with no materialised entity.created event, read the plan file's YAML frontmatter directly to populate entities.attributes. Masks the gap created by commits that emit entity.completed without prior entity.created. Routing in the flow view now finds the correct milestone/t2_parent for all 9 M1 T3s. Underlying methodology rule captured separately as inbox item.

attributes.text: Architecture pivot: browser-direct to Anthropic API + thin server wrapper, instead of the inbox item's proposed claude-CLI-via-server. Browser-direct keeps API credentials with the user's account (no server-side key store), makes the cost model transparent, and makes summaries durable across sessions via localStorage. The server wrapper shrinks to three endpoints (clean-check, save-summary, invalidate-summary) — git state + filesystem only, no LLM credentials. Additional scope captured in T2-analyser that the inbox item didn't have: summaries as first-class events (analysis.live-summary, analysis.invalidated), per-summary markdown files, clean-tree guard for sequencing within commits, cascade invalidation, bulk mode with Anthropic prompt caching, flow-view rendering of saved summaries. Superseding the inbox item rather than amending it because the design delta is substantial — the inbox proposal could not have evolved into this without rewriting; preserving the original as a fulcrum'd dead node is honest history.

attributes.summary: Four design refinements from review pass: (1) Programmatic context building (§3.12) — browser walks projection+cache to pre-assemble per-entity context bundle (focal plan + 1-hop graph + open blockers/HITL + inbox refs + prior summary chain); agent never does discovery. ~30-50% input-token saving vs agentic-discovery. (2) Opportunistic derived caching (§3.13) — primary analysis on E also emits structured summaries for 1-hop dependents touched; saved as source:derived events with origin_summary_event_id; primary always supersedes derived, derived never supersedes primary. Cheap drive-by refreshes on dependents without extra input-token cost. (3) Global update mode (§3.8 reframed) — merged with bulk mode; explicit whole-graph-as-primaries pass; derived emission suppressed since every entity gets a primary anyway. (4) Cost-warning dialog (§3.9.1) — every Claude call gated by input/output token estimate + dollar cost confirmation; global mode uses red accent; estimator calibration recorded per save. Phases A and B grew; total time ~9h (was ~7-8h). Three new swap-out points + four new open questions captured.
